tooling: the user installs and runs the qwen CLI (npm package @qwen-code/qwen-code, which needs Node.js 22 or later, or the vendor's standalone install script) on any machine, rented or free ones included, and gives it an endpoint key
chaining: the agent pairs with a key of a built-in provider (DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, Requesty) or with any OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini compatible endpoint, so a free endpoint recorded under inference makes the whole stack free; the key-free Qwen OAuth route closed on 2026-04-15
reliability_note: the vendor cut the free Qwen OAuth quota from 1,000 to 100 requests per day and closed the route on 2026-04-15; cached OAuth tokens may work briefly and new requests are rejected

free_tier.stated: open-source agent for the terminal; bring an OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini compatible key; the free Qwen OAuth route was discontinued on 2026-04-15
free_tier.notes: the agent costs nothing; the key it is given is the bill

interface_detail: a terminal agent; multi-protocol, so any OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini compatible base URL works
limits_note: no quota binds the agent itself; the provider of the chosen endpoint serves and meters the usage, among them the vendor's QwenCloud (a Token Plan with a monthly Credit quota, or a pay-as-you-go Standard API Key) and Alibaba ModelStudio (a Coding Plan with a weekly quota); the free Qwen OAuth route closed on 2026-04-15

identity_cost.detail: none to install or run the CLI; the npm package and the standalone install script download with no credential, and each endpoint key carries that endpoint's own registration cost; the qwen.ai account was needed only for the Qwen OAuth route, closed on 2026-04-15

confidence_note: the vendor's auth documentation states the end of the free OAuth tier and the current /auth routes; the anonymous install path was measured with unauthenticated GETs of the npm tarball and the install script; capacity belongs to the endpoint chosen and is not measured here
